BUSN 1990.attendance: Regular attendance is required for a satisfactory grade because there are relatively few class sessions; difficulties meeting this must be discussed with the instructor.

objectives: Students will learn Porter’s five forces, which will be used as a lens to view the different industries and case studies presented throughout the semester.
Students will learn about Mergers and Acquisitions and the institutions involved in those financial transactions.
Subsequently, students will compare private and public institutions that are affected by the financial institutions previously discussed.
Students will learn management consultants' roles in advising and solving problems for companies.
Students will learn about leadership and business ethics and corporate social responsibility.
Students will learn how important each of the different institutions' work is to one another, as well as explain how they all work together.
topics: Introduction Case Study Analysis Business Leader Presentations Fundamental Valuation Financial Institution Valuation Rev

objectives: Upon completion of course, each student should be able to identify what is meant by sustainable business.
Upon completion of course, each student should be able to understand the main issues related to sustainable business.
Upon completion of course, each student should be able to explain how a business could be "responsible" while also being profitable.

Upon completion of course, each student should be prepared to bring their knowledge of sustainability issues to their future business studies and their understanding of business to address issues in sustainability.
topics: Identifying a sustainable business How could sustainable businesses ever be profitable?
Reporting on sustainable business performance Examples of sustainability across the business curriculum
